title: Shrine telling detail
_note: A small, specific sign of recent (or long-past) attention — the line that makes a shrine feel lived-with. Lowercase noun phrases, composed after the condition.

entries.value: a guttering candle left by a recent pilgrim
a scatter of offering-coins
a ring of melted wax
picked-clean bones at its foot
a wilted garland
prayers scratched into the stone
an empty offering bowl
fresh footprints in the dust around it
dried bloodstains on the stone
faded ribbons tied to it
a single fresh-cut flower
a heap of small cairns left by travellers
a stick of incense still trailing smoke
a cup of wine gone sour
a rusted knife driven into the earth before it
a child's shoe left among the offerings
coins hammered into cracks in the stone
a red ochre handprint, still bright
a lock of hair knotted around it
a ring of animal skulls on stakes
a little votive figure of woven straw
a new name carved over a chiselled-out one
a scattering of yellowed teeth
a folded prayer-slip pinned beneath a pebble
a fresh smear of blood, not yet dry
a small heap of scattered salt
a broken sword laid before it
a fetish of feathers and bone bound with sinew
fresh claw-marks raked across it
a single eye freshly painted on the stone
a trail of spilled grain leading to it
a wax figure stuck through with pins
the ashes of a recent fire before it
knee-prints pressed in the mud before it
a votive plaque of hammered tin, newly hung
a doll bound tight in red thread
a chalk sigil drawn fresh on the ground
clay pilgrim-tokens hung from a nearby branch
the lingering smell of incense
a knot of braided grain left to rot
